'''Taichiro Shiraishi''' (白石 太一郎, ''Shiraishi Taichiro'', born November 14, 1938<ref>''Yomiuri Yearbook 2016'' (Yomiuri Shimbun Tokyo, 2016) p. 321</ref>) is a Japanese archaeologist and honorary professor at the {{ill|National Museum of Japanese History|en|National Museum of Japanese History|qid=Q3330690|lt=National Museum of Japanese History}} and {{ill|The Graduate University for Advanced Studies|en|The Graduate University for Advanced Studies|qid=Q2983844|lt=The Graduate University for Advanced Studies}}. He is also an honorary director of the {{ill|Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum|ff|Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum|fr|Musée préfectoral Chikatsu Asuka d'Osaka|ja|大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館|pt|Museu Histórico Chikatsu-Asuka|uk|Осацький префектурний музей Тікацу-Асука|zh|大阪府立近飛鳥博物館|qid=Q4557237|lt=Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum}}.

== Career ==
Shiraishi was born in Osaka City, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} in 1938. After graduating from [[Osaka Seiko Gakuin Junior and Senior High School|Osaka Seiko Academy High School]], he completed a degree in cultural history at the [[Doshisha University Faculty of Letters]] in 1961. He continued his studies in the graduate program at the same university, completing a master's degree in 1964 before leaving the doctoral program without completing his degree in 1968.

He became a researcher at the [[Ancient Studies Association]] in April 1968 and began working at the [[Kashihara Archaeological Institute]] in August 1969. In 1978, he was appointed an investigator at the establishment preparation office of the {{ill|National Museum of Japanese History|en|National Museum of Japanese History|qid=Q3330690|lt=National Museum of Japanese History}} under the [[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] to help establish the museum. When the museum opened in 1981, he became an associate professor. In 1984, he was promoted to professor (also serving as a professor at the {{ill|The Graduate University for Advanced Studies|en|The Graduate University for Advanced Studies|qid=Q2983844|lt=The Graduate University for Advanced Studies}}) and later became the deputy director of the museum. He retired in 2004 and was named professor emeritus. Afterward, he served as a professor at the Faculty of Letters at {{ill|Nara University|en|Nara University|qid=Q8190036|lt=Nara University}} from April 2004 until his retirement in 2009, later becoming the honorary director of the {{ill|Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum|ff|Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum|fr|Musée préfectoral Chikatsu Asuka d'Osaka|ja|大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館|pt|Museu Histórico Chikatsu-Asuka|uk|Осацький префектурний музей Тікацу-Асука|zh|大阪府立近飛鳥博物館|qid=Q4557237|lt=Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum}}.<ref>[https://www.sankei.com/article/20170726-7DXMKHCUYRJV3OCZFT7LW2GOHA/ Shiraishi Taichiro, Director of the Osaka Prefectural Chikatsu Asuka Museum: "Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Cluster, World Heritage Value is Significant" (Sankei Shimbun)]</ref>

Shiraishi has also served as a visiting professor at the {{ill|Open University of Japan|en|Open University of Japan|qid=Q15501569|lt=Open University of Japan}} and other institutions and has held roles on cultural property preservation committees, such as the [[Agency for Cultural Affairs]]' committee for the permanent preservation of the murals of the {{ill|Takamatsuzuka Tomb|en|Takamatsuzuka Tomb|qid=Q1039675|lt=Takamatsuzuka Tomb}}.

== Awards ==
* 2002: Archaeology Prize from [[Yuzankaku Publishing]].
* 2020: Recognition for contributions to regional culture.<ref>[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodoha11yo/pdf/92732301_02.pdf 2020 Regional Cultural Contributors List]</ref>

== Research and Contributions ==
Shiraishi specializes in Japanese archaeology, focusing on the formation processes of ancient Japanese states and culture.

=== Views ===
* He is a proponent of the [[Yamatai Koku|Kinki Theory]] concerning the location of {{ill|Yamatai|en|Yamatai|qid=Q844295|lt=Yamatai}}.
* Based on studies of pottery distribution during the Yamatai period, Shiraishi has suggested that the {{nihongo|Jinmu Expedition|神武東征|Jinmu tōsei}} legend may not be historical.<ref>Japanese History Volume 1: ''The Birth of Yamato,'' edited by Taichiro Shiraishi, 2002, ISBN 4-642-00801-2</ref>
* He has proposed that the {{nihongo|Hashihaka Kofun|箸墓古墳}} was the tomb of [[Himiko]] and that the nearby {{nihongo|Nishimiya-no-zuka Kofun|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} in Tenri City could be the tomb of [[Toyosukiirihime|Toyo]].<ref>''Between Archaeology and Ancient History,'' 2004, Chikuma Shobō, ISBN 4-480-04254-7</ref>
